subject: emit namespace imports for standalone declarations in remote scopes
body:
When an `NgModule` imports or re-exports an in-program standalone declaration, ngtsc resolves its scope entry from the declaration's own metadata rather than the import identifier in the module file, so remote scoping emits it through a namespace import.

Previously the preprocessor kept the module file's local import alias on the reference, causing `ɵɵsetComponentScope` to emit the bare identifier instead. These changes strip the importer aliases for non-`.d.ts` standalone declarations in `NgModule` scopes to match ngtsc.

Also fixes a couple of tests that were failing due to formatting.

subject: enable passing tests
body: A few of the `@defer` block validation tests were passing, but were producing more diagnostics than ngtsc. The amount of diagnostics was an implementation detail so these changes update the assertions and enable the tests. Also moves one partial compilation test into a different bucket.

subject: run all ngtsc tests against preprocessor
body: Some ngtsc tests weren't running against the preprocessor. These changes enable them and add the failures to the known failures.

subject: suppress inheritance errors for metadata in preprocessor
body: Fixes an issue that popped up internally where if we generated `ctorParameters` or `propDecorators` for a base class, we end triggering a `noImplicitOverride` error on the child class. These changes resolve it by adding a `@ts-ignore`.

subject: expand same-file imports arrays in preprocessor
avoid compilation errors for invalid tracking functions
body: Fixes that when we generate code for an `@for` tracking function we had references to variables in a different scope. Now we produce a placeholder expression instead and let the template type checker flag the issues.

subject: avoid producing type errors for invalid `@let` usages
body: Previous we produced `undefined` when an `@let` was referenced incorrectly. This can cause type issues when the generated code is typed checked so instead we use the `invalid` instruction.

subject: introduce placeholder instruction for invalid expressions
body: Adds the `ɵɵinvalid` instruction that we can use in places where an expression is used incorrectly, but we can't drop it without affecting the template's logic.

subject: emit untyped inline input transforms in local mode
body: Matches ngtsc's behavior in the preprocessor by preserving inline decorator input transform functions even when their first parameter does not have an explicit type annotation.

subject: port custom decorator validation in local mode
body: Ports over the custom decorator validations from ngtsc to the preprocessor.

subject: validate host directive in local compilation
body: Matches ngtsc's validation for host directives in the preprocessor.

subject: add validation for defer in local compilation mode
body: Sets up the validations for `@defer` in local compilation mode within the preprocessor.

subject: generate extra imports in local compilation mode
body: Matches ngtsc's behavior for generating extra imports when local compilation mode is enabled in the preprocessor.

subject: validate constants in local mode
body: Ports over the logic for the `LOCAL_COMPILATION_UNRESOLVED_CONST` validations from ngtsc.

subject: enable more passing tests
body: Enables more tests that pass in the preprocessor, aside from some minor formatting differences.

subject: release notes for the v22.2.4 release
initial implementation of incremental compilation in preprocessor
body:
Adds an initial implementation for incremental compilation in the preprocessor. Some numbers from a benchmark running against a synthetic app made up of  20 features x 20 components + 30 shared directives/pipes/services (~500 TS files, ~400 templates):

| scenario | main | branch | delta | files processed (main -> branch) | files written (main -> branch) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cold build (fresh analyzer) | 3388 ms | **3366 ms** | −0.7% | 513 -> 513 | 513 -> 513 |
| rebuild: template edit (leaf component) | 3143 ms | **41 ms** | −98.7% | 513 -> 1 | 513 -> 1 |
| rebuild: component method

subject: describe the prerender.format option in the SSR guide
update test types
body: Fixes a test failure due to out of date typings.

subject: disallow bindings to on* properties in preprocessor
body: Ports the logic from ngtsc that prevents users from binding to `on*` events.

subject: enable passing tests
body: Enables a few tests that were passing, aside from overly-aggressive assertions.

subject: deduplicate pipe diagnostics in preprocessor
body: Matches ngtsc's behavior that de-duplicates OOB diagnostics on pipes.

subject: inline type constructor when dependency are in the same file
body: Fixes some failing preprocessor tests by enabling inline type constructors when a directive and a component that depends on it are in the same file and the TCB is inlined.

subject: do not emit new namespace imports for DI dependencies
body:
Currently when something is injected, we produce a namespace import (e.g. `import * as i1`) to match ngtsc's behavior. This ends up breaking some internal builds.

These changes switch to referencing those symbols directly.

subject: preserve isolated NgModule imports in emitDeclarationOnly mode
body:
Previously, in `--emitDeclarationOnly` mode, external identifiers in
`@NgModule.imports` and `exports` were dropped from `ɵmod` type arguments
if their value expressions could not be statically evaluated within the
current file.

Now `ng-analyze` extracts raw identifier references (including spread
elements and forwardRefs) from `imports` and `exports`, and `processor.ts`
preserves unresolved value-position imports so they can be emitted as
`typeof ExternalModule` in the `.d.ts` `ɵɵNgModuleDeclaration` type.

subject: always validate component hostDirectives and poison on error
body:
Validates component `hostDirectives` before scope resolution so that
standalone components with invalid `imports` or orphan non-standalone
components still report `hostDirectives` diagnostics, poisons the class
when `hostDirectives` validation fails, and suppresses cascading
component/directive diagnostics when `hostDirectives` has a structural
shape error (`NG1010`), matching `ngtsc`.

subject: resolve @Input transform first-parameter types in coercion members
body:
Resolves the first-parameter type of local, imported, and `@angular/core`
(`booleanAttribute`, `numberAttribute`) transform functions in Stage 2
when the parameter type is emittable/self-contained or absent, emitting
the resolved type directly in `static ngAcceptInputType_<input>` instead
of `Parameters<typeof fn>[0]`.

subject: emit ɵsetClassMetadata after class when custom decorators exist
body:
When a class has non-Angular class decorators, TypeScript compiles those
decorators into `MyClass = __decorate([...], MyClass)` after the class
body. Emitting `ɵsetClassMetadata` inside the static initializer block
attaches metadata to the original class before `__decorate` potentially
replaces it.

Now `ngp` detects non-Angular class decorators and emits the
`ɵsetClassMetadata` IIFE immediately after the class declaration, matching
`ngtsc`.

subject: downlevel jit: true Angular member and parameter decorators
body:
Previously, when a directive or component used `jit: true`, `ngp` emitted
`static ctorParameters` but left member decorators (`@Input`, `@Output`,
`@ViewChild`, etc.) and constructor parameter decorators (`@Optional`,
`@Inject`, etc.) attached in the preprocessed output.

Now `ng-analyze` collects `decorator_removal_spans` for Angular constructor
parameter and identifier-named member decorators on `jit: true` classes, and
`processFileSync` strips those decorators and emits `static propDecorators`.

subject: fix remaining NGP compliance test failures
body:
Fix the remaining known NGP compliance failures across full compile and
declaration-only emission modes:

- Forward baseUrl and paths from compiler options into synthetic tsconfig in ngp_test_driver.ts.
- Classify quoted string literal property keys in @HostBinding and @HostListener as ExpressionValueKind::String so @angular/compiler generates KeyedRead instead of PropertyRead.
- Make PipeMetadata.name an optional string rather than falling back to class_name when unnamed, emitting null in ɵɵPipeDeclaration.
- In declaration-only emit, emit external module references (i<N>.X) for external refe

subject: share a single ImportManager for CopySourceToTcb shims
body:
In `InliningMode.CopySourceToTcb`, `TypeCheckContextImpl.executeOperations`
previously instantiated a separate `ImportManager` for the copied source
content, while `TypeCheckFile.render()` finalized a second `ImportManager`
initialized against an empty `contextFile` for the same `.ngtypecheck.ts`
shim. This caused:
1. Conflicting namespace import identifiers (`i0`) when both inline TCB
   operations and `TypeCheckFile` emitted namespace imports into the same
   shim file.
2. Duplicate imports for modules already present in the copied source (such
   as `@angular/core`).
3. Potential collisions

subject: reject unsupported updateOn in SignalFormControl
body:
Signal forms are model-driven and do not support pending or uncommitted
values. As a result, non-default `updateOn` options (`blur`, `submit`)
cannot be supported.

This commit adds a dev-mode check in `SignalFormControl` to throw an error
when:
1. An unsupported `updateOn` option is passed directly in options to the
   `SignalFormControl` constructor.
2. A non-default `updateOn` option is inherited from a parent `FormGroup`
   or `FormArray` via `setParent()`.

Additionally, `SignalFormControl` explicitly overrides `get updateOn()`
to return `'change'`.

subject: do not treat outputs named class or style as styling inputs
body:
When a directive had an output whose public name is `class` or `style`,
the node was flagged as having a directive input with that name. The
template's `[class]` or `[style]` binding was then sent to directive
inputs instead of the element, found none, and its value was silently
dropped. Interpolated `class`/`style` attributes and host directives
that expose such an output were affected as well.

subject: support direct component param
body: Allows skipping undefined extras arg.

subject: update  RouterTestingHarness documentation
body: Updating RouterTestingHarness documentation to include `navigate` method

subject: add navigate method to RouterTestingHarness
body:
Mirrors `Router.navigate` so tests can pass `queryParams`, `fragment` and other
`NavigationExtras` without an extra navigation.

subject: correctly inherit component metadata in JIT undecorated base classes
body:
When a bare class extends a component, the JIT compiler compiles it as an abstract directive. Previously, this caused the compiler to skip inheriting the component's metadata into the bare class due to an incorrect throw, or the bare class was skipped completely because `getDirectiveDef` looked up the prototype chain.

This commit updates the `addDirectiveDefToUndecoratedParents` helper to use `Object.hasOwn` to ensure bare classes receive their own `ɵdir` containing their inputs/outputs, and updates `ɵɵInheritDefinitionFeature` to permit these abstract directives to inherit from components.

subject: use official webmcp-types
body: Vendor the official `webmcp-types` instead of `@mcp-b/webmcp-types`.

subject: surface preprocessor wasm engine errors as Error instances
body:
The wasm engine's fallible exports (`analyze*`, `updateFileContent`,
`invalidateFiles`, `setEntryPoints`, `getFileContent`) return
`Result<_, String>`, which wasm-bindgen throws across the boundary as a bare
string. `WasmAnalyzer` forwarded those unchanged, so a failed call rejected
with a string on the wasm backend but with an `Error` on the N-API backend
(`napi::Error`) and the sidecar backend (`new Error(payload)`). Consumers of
`IAnalyzer` that inspect `error.message`, `instanceof Error` or `.stack` —
and test matchers such as `toBeRejectedWithError` — therefore behaved
differently dependi

subject: decouple preprocessor syntax extraction from resource and module resolution
body:
Previously, `QueryEngine::analyze_file_syntax_body` held the `ParsedFile` mutex guard across the
entire single-file syntax pass, including `@angular/core` package detection, external component
template and stylesheet loading via `ResourceResolver`, and static and dynamic import specifier
resolution. Because `std::sync::MutexGuard<ParsedFile>` cannot be held across `.await` points,
coupling AST traversal to synchronous filesystem reads and module resolution prevented replacing
direct resolver and filesystem access with an asynchronous bundler host protocol.

Make `analyze_parsed`, `ClassVisitor

subject: expand preprocessor no-tsconfig test coverage
body:
The options-only form of `createAnalyzer` (no `tsconfigPath`) was only exercised
end-to-end for a single standalone component. The behaviors that actually depend
on the root list and on options that would otherwise come from the tsconfig —
NgModule scope resolution, root replacement via `setEntryPoints`, the
`r3SymbolsFile` override and `PrefixImportStrategy` — were covered by Rust unit
tests alone, not through the public API and the wasm transport that hosts
without a tsconfig use.

Add WASM end-to-end test cases for running the preprocessor without a
`tsconfig.json`:

- Resolving `NgModule`

subject: avoid mutating recorded frames when merging a frame range
body:
When a later frame has a directive that the first selected frame doesn't,
`mergeFrames` added that frame's directive object to the merged result
by reference. Merging the next frame then added its timings into the
recorded frame, so selecting three or more frames inflated the stored
change detection and lifecycle times, and they grew each time the range
was selected again.

Copy the directive before adding it to the merged result.

Tested by adding a spec that merges three frames and checks that the
input frames are unchanged.

subject: update generated file names in the ecosystem guides
body:
The web worker, service worker and app shell guides still showed `app.component.*` file names and the old root template text. Use the current names (`app.ts`, `app.html`, `app-shell.ts`), the current root template text, and list the files the generated `ngsw-config.json`
actually caches.

body: Adding some feedback based on AI security reports to help guide them towards what is and is not a legitimate vulnerability.

subject: move language service helpers out of the preprocessor core
body:
`src/comments.ts` and `src/tcb_ls_util.ts` are only used by the preprocessor language service
(and the VS Code extension server built on it), but they live in `src/`, so the `preprocessor`
target's `src/**` glob ships them with the core compiler. They are also the only two files in
that target that import `typescript` directly: the compiler itself never touches it, and the
analyzer reads the tsconfig in Rust. Moving them into `language-service/src/` leaves the core
sources free of direct TypeScript imports and keeps the helpers next to their consumers.

Neither file is part of the public API:

subject: widen type on viewport instructions
body: Widens the type on the instructions accepting `IntersectionObserverInit` since this causes duplicate diagnostics when the preprocessor is enabled. We type check this properly in the TCB.

subject: write the preprocessor `.ngdiag.json` once per run
body:
`run` wrote `<tsconfig>.ngdiag.json` after every analysis chunk and then once more after the
loop. The per-chunk write dates from the initial import and never had a consumer: nothing reads
the file while `ngp` is running, and build integrations only read it after a successful exit.
The trailing write was added later so that option diagnostics still reach the file when the
analyzer produces no chunks, which left N + 1 writes whose last two are byte-identical, each
re-sorting and re-serializing every diagnostic collected so far. The in-place overwrite is also
not atomic, so the extra writes only

subject: document deploying localized apps with prerendering
body:
Add a "Prerendering" section to the i18n deploy guide for apps built with
`outputMode: "static"`. It describes the per-locale output layout, serving
the source locale from the root with `"subPath": ""`, the lack of
`Accept-Language` redirects without a server, and per-locale not-found pages.

Also add a short section to the locale ID guide on reading the active locale
with `$localize.locale` where `LOCALE_ID` can't be injected.

subject: unconditionally use namespace imports for imported constructor tokens in ngp
body:
Align ngp with ngtsc by unconditionally emitting imported constructor
DI tokens and class metadata through module namespace imports (e.g.
i1.Service) instead of only doing so for @angular/core or in
complianceMode.

This removes the divergence and eliminates the need to pass complianceMode
to buildDeps or useCoreNamespace/complianceMode to buildCtorParametersExpr.

subject: decouple preprocessor HybridCompiler from tsconfigPath
body:
`HybridCompiler` wrote `<tsconfig>.ngdiag.json` itself from `prepareChunk` and `prepareChunkSync`,
which tied it to a `tsconfigPath` and to the Node filesystem, or to a `virtualFiles` overlay
standing in for it. Now that the analyzer no longer requires a tsconfig, hosts that embed the
compiler without one have nowhere to write such a file, and whether and where diagnostics are
persisted is a decision for the build driver rather than for the compiler.

`tsconfigPath` and `virtualFiles` are therefore removed from `HybridCompilerOptions`, together
with `writeDiagnosticsFile` and `writeDiagnostics

subject: update cross-repo adev docs
body: Updated Angular adev cross repo docs files.

subject: fix inaccurate null and class notes in the template binding guide
body:
Interpolation renders null and undefined as an empty string instead of
converting them with toString. Attribute bindings remove the attribute for
undefined as well as null. The [class] binding does not drop strings that
are not valid CSS class names, so describe the string form instead.

subject: match ctorParameters behavior from ngtsc
body: Resolves a test failure internally where we weren't matching how ngtsc emits `ctorParameters` for primitive types. It appears that in ngtsc we have some logic where `string` gets emitted as the `String` object, `number` as the `Number` object etc.

subject: enforce declaration-only emission diagnostics in preprocessor
body:
Pass through `compilerOptions.emitDeclarationOnly` and `angularCompilerOptions._experimentalAllowEmitDeclarationOnly` into `ng-analyze` and enforce the diagnostics required in experimental declaration-only emission mode:
- Reject custom class decorators with `NG1005` (`DECORATOR_UNEXPECTED`) and skip trait compilation for those classes without affecting standard dev-mode builds.
- Report `NG1010` (`VALUE_HAS_WRONG_TYPE`) when an inline `@Input` transform function has an untyped or spread first parameter.
- Report `NG11003` (`LOCAL_COMPILATION_UNSUPPORTED_EXPRESSION`) when a `hostDirectives` en

subject: migrate compliance test expectations to full-file goldens
body:
Migrate the ngtsc compliance test suite from snippet-based golden files to full-file golden files:

subject: make tsconfig optional for the preprocessor analyzer
body:
Integrations such as bundlers and the Angular CLI may have no tsconfig at all, or already own
the parsed configuration. The analyzer can now be constructed from options alone.

`AnalyzerOptions.tsconfigPath` is now optional, and three options replace what could
previously only come from the tsconfig:

- `entryPoints`: the roots of the program closure. When set, they replace the tsconfig's root
  files, and the roots are no longer re-read from the tsconfig after file updates (the same
  holds after `setEntryPoints`). Bundlers pass their own entry files; the analyzer follows
  imports from there

subject: fix inaccurate notes in the forms guides
body:
The validators snippet used an inline Validators.pattern call that
removeValidators can never match, because Angular compares validators by
reference. The signal forms guides said that dirty compares the value
with its initial state, that debounce('blur') has no effect without a
touch output (the value is never written to the form model), and that
only hidden and disabled fields skip validation.

subject: keep focus in the API reference filter
body:
The API reference filter writes its value to the URL on each change. With
the Navigation API integration, each of these navigations ends with the
browser moving focus to the body, so typing `signal` in the filter leaves
`s` and the other keys go to the page.

Pass `focusReset: 'manual'` next to `scroll: 'manual'`, so focus stays in
the filter field.

subject: add focusReset to NavigationBehaviorOptions
body:
With the platform navigation integration, the router passes `scroll` to
`NavigateEvent#intercept()` but not `focusReset`, so the browser moves
focus to the body after every navigation. A search field that writes its
value to a query param loses focus after the first key.

Add a `focusReset` option next to `scroll` and pass it to `intercept()`,
so a navigation can leave focus where it is. Without the option, the
browser default still applies.

Fixes #71594

subject: skip split when piercing empty path outlets
body:
`split` is designed to split remaining primary outlet segments alongside
empty-path named outlets (`createChildrenForEmptyPaths` wraps `slicedSegments`
in `res[PRIMARY_OUTLET]`). When piercing an empty-path route to look for a
named outlet among its descendants (`!matchedOnOutlet`), `remainingSegments`
belong to that named outlet rather than `PRIMARY_OUTLET`.

Previously, `split` was called even when `!matchedOnOutlet`, which required
the `isSelfEvaluating` workaround in #67708 to ignore an empty-path route for
the same outlet being evaluated. However, if the pierced empty-path route also
cont

subject: migrate static string and array ngClass bindings to class
body:
The ngclass-to-class migration only looked at object literals, so bindings
like `[ngClass]="'first second'"` and `[ngClass]="['first', 'second']"` were
left untouched even though `[class]` accepts exactly the same shapes. See
`toStylingKeyValueArray` in packages/core/src/render3/instructions/styling.ts,
which handles `string | string[] | Set<string> | {[key: string]: any}`.

Both forms are now forwarded to `[class]` unchanged. Detection goes through
the TypeScript parser rather than matching quotes, so an expression that
merely starts and ends with a quote - a ternary, a concatenation - is not

subject: update ambient module specifier check for Oxc 0.155
body:
#71606 added `resolve_ambient_module_member` comparing `decl.id.value.as_str()`
directly against `&str`, and landed shortly before #71599 upgraded `oxc_*` to
0.155.0 (where `StringLiteral::value` is now `oxc_str::JSStr`, whose `.as_str()`
returns `Option<&str>`).

Use `js_str_to_string_lossy(decl.id.value)` consistently with the other
`StringLiteral::value` call sites updated in #71599.

subject: improve the warning for bindings on elements inside ICU expressions
body:
Directives and bindings are not supported on elements inside ICU
expressions, because ICU content is processed at runtime as plain HTML.
Using one anyway, e.g. `<b [title]="title">` inside a plural case, used to
crash with a cryptic `InvalidCharacterError` from `setAttribute`. Since the
ICU attribute allowlist was introduced, such attributes are dropped with a
generic "ignoring unknown attribute name" warning that points to the XSS
security guide, which doesn't tell developers what is actually wrong.

Detect binding-like attribute names (`[prop]`, `(event)`, `*structural`,
`#ref`, `@trigger`)

subject: don't report diagnostics against .d.ts files in preprocessor
body:
Fixes that referencing a non-class from a declaration file in an `NgModule` (e.g. passing `NgModule` itself into `imports`) produced a diagnostic pointing to the `.d.ts` file. There were two problems:
1. The evaluator was resolving a type reference to anything it could find, whereas ngtsc only resolves it if the target is a class. As a result, `declare const NgModule: NgModuleDecorator` was resolving to the interface instead of the variable.
2. ngtsc keeps diagnostics on `.d.ts` files, but they're never reported if the build only asks for the diagnostics of the compilation unit's source files,

subject: correctly classify DI tokens from ambient modules

subject: fix the NgOptimizedImage sizes and decoding notes
body:
NgOptimizedImage prepends auto to sizes only for lazy-loaded images, and
it always sets decoding to sync on priority images, ignoring an explicit
decoding value. The guide implied both applied to every image.

body:
close() left the channel of the last start in place, and the connect
handler only sets a channel up when there is none. A listen() after
close(), or after a listen() whose channel setup failed (which closes
the server), connected without consuming and never called back. The
stale channel also made connection failures count as a reconnect, so
"maxConnectionAttempts" was never reached.

Reset the channel at the start of each listen, like the attempt counter.

match route paths without a leading slash as express does (#18298)
body:
find-my-way reads the first character of a route path as its leading "/",
so the "{*any}" route @nestjs/serve-static registers for the fallback of
a single-page app became find-my-way's "*" route, whose wildcard the
route table then rejected for every request: client-side routes got a
404. A route path that does not start with "/" is now matched with
path-to-regexp, as Express matches it ("{*any}" matches every path, and
"users" never matches "/users"). Routes Nest registers always start with
"/" and stay in the tree.

subject: check the sse pending data limit after each write
body:
An SSE client whose stream is backed up is dropped once more event data
waits for it than the route's "maxPendingDataLength" allows. The limit
was only checked when the producer emitted an event. A producer that
emits many events at once, synchronously (e.g. replaying past events
before live ones), emits them all before the first write can back the
stream up, and none after, so they waited in memory for a client that
never read them, past the limit.

subject: bound how long a tcp packet may take to arrive
body:
A packet's declared length was never compared against "maxBufferSize",
so a packet that could never be accepted was still buffered until the
buffer filled up. It is now rejected as soon as its length is read, and
the connection is dropped, since everything that follows is the rest of
that packet.

The idle timer for a partially received packet is refreshed on every
read, so a peer that sends a few bytes now and then kept a partial
packet buffered for as long as it liked. The new "messageReceiveTimeout"
option (default: 300000ms, like "requestTimeout" in node:http) bounds
the time from a packet

body:
The disconnect specs read the tick count right after the client destroyed its socket, but the server only sees the disconnect once the socket close reaches it. Under load the producer's 20 ms interval could tick once more in between, so the count was off by one (7 of 12 runs failed under full CPU load).

The producer now records its teardown, and the specs take the count once it has happened. They still fail when the producer is never stopped.

body:
BaseRpcExceptionFilter sent the error held by an RpcException as it is
whenever it was an object. For an Error, as in new RpcException(err),
the client then got the enumerable properties of the Error (such as the
request config of an HTTP client error) or its toJSON() output.

is logged, and the client gets the "Internal server error" payload.
Plain objects and strings are sent as before.

subject: treat an error in a ws exception as unknown
body:
BaseWsExceptionFilter sent the error held by a WsException as it is
whenever it was an object. For an Error, as in new WsException(err),
the client then got the enumerable properties of the Error (such as the
request config of an HTTP client error) or its toJSON() output.

An Error held by a WsException is now handled as an unknown error: it is
logged, and the client gets the "Internal server error" payload, with
its cause. Plain objects and strings are sent as before.

subject: target the current Node.js version for server builds, remove the hardcoded `26.0.0` clamp (AI-assisted) (#12781)
body:
SWC no longer falls back to ES5 for Node.js versions newer than its
Browserslist data: it now skips all transforms for them, like Babel
(swc-project/swc#11457, shipped in every Rspack 2.x).

The server target is the current Node.js version without its pre-release
tag, because SWC panics on versions like "27.0.0-rc.1".

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: evict the bundler persistent cache when the target browsers, the server Node.js target or plugin versions change (AI-assisted) (#12774)
body:
The persistent cache doesn't track loader options, so getCacheVersion()
must include what they're computed from:

- The targets from the new getTargets(): the browsers the client queries
  match, instead of the queries. The same queries (like "baseline widely
  available") can match other browsers over time or after a Browserslist
  data upgrade. For the server cache, the server targets (current Node.js
  version or DOCUSAURUS_SERVER_NODE_TARGET).
- The plugin versions: upgrading a third-party plugin can change the
  loader options it computes without changing any build dependency.

Co-authore

- Structure code as a tree: a high-level function first, delegating to

- Make the intent explicit with well-named variables and functions,
  grouped related lines, and pure functions
- Favor readability over micro-optimizations outside hot paths

code change.

subject: install pnpm with pnpm/setup instead of pnpm/action-setup (AI-assisted) (#12657)
body:
* chore(ci): install pnpm with pnpm/setup instead of pnpm/action-setup (AI-assisted)

pnpm/action-setup v6.0.10 runs `npm ci` for a pnpm v11 bootstrap, then
self-updates to the packageManager version (pnpm 12.3.4). pnpm/setup
downloads the native pnpm executable from the npm registry and verifies
it against npm's signature. The step drops from ~16s to ~2s on Windows
and from ~6s to ~1s on Linux.

pnpm/setup always restores and saves a lockfile verification cache.
Privileged workflows block it with `cache-mode: none`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Restoring the pnpm store cache on Windows runners takes 20-80s (tar + zstd
extraction), while it saves 0-8s on "pnpm install". On a cache miss, saving
the cache adds another 10-15s. Disable it for the E2E Windows and Windows
Tests jobs.

subject: use 10-char content hashes in JS/CSS filenames to avoid RealContentHash false positives (AI-assisted) (#12641)
body:
* fix(core): use 10-char content hashes in JS/CSS filenames to avoid RealContentHash false positives (AI-assisted)

Webpack and Rspack RealContentHashPlugin replace every occurrence of a
provisional [contenthash:8] in all assets, including inside unrelated hex
strings: file-loader asset names, colors, numbers. The client and server
compilations do it independently, so a false positive can make the SSG HTML
reference a file that doesn't exist (404 image). On the Docusaurus website
that's ~1 expected false positive per 32 full builds; 10 chars makes it
~1 in 9,300. Rsbuild uses the same default

body:
## Problem

`EGITNOPERMISSION` interpolates `options.repositoryUrl` into the error
`details`. By the time this error is thrown (`index.js`, after
`verifyAuth` fails), `options.repositoryUrl` has been replaced with the
result of `getGitAuthUrl()`, which can embed CI credentials (`GH_TOKEN`,
`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GL_TOKEN`, `BB_TOKEN`, …) as basic-auth in the URL.

subject: publish through npm trusted publishing (#1560)
body:
The release job authenticates to npm through OIDC: it gets `id-token: write` and no
`npm-token`, and `actions/setup-node` no longer takes `registry-url`, whose placeholder
`_authToken` in `.npmrc` would shadow the OIDC flow. pnpm 12 exchanges the token itself,
and the npm of Node.js 26 from `.tool-versions` is newer than the 11.5.1 that trusted
publishing needs. The release job lists `contents: write` too, since a job with
permissions gets no others.

subject: don't crash on a commit type named after an Object.prototype member (#1559)
body:
Commit groups were collected into a plain object, so a `__proto__` or `constructor` type
found an inherited value instead of a group and the writer threw. The accumulator has no
prototype now.

Fixes #1544

subject: parse reference actions of footers followed by a colon (#1558)
body:
A footer token may be followed by a colon, as in `Closes: <issue>`. The parser took such a
line for a footer but not for a reference action, so its reference had no action and kept
the token in `raw`. Footer lines now take an optional colon after the keyword, while the
header and the sentences of the body still need whitespace, since `fix:` is also a type.

The conventionalcommits preset renders these references under `closes` now, and its test
expects that.

subject: match reference actions as whole words (#1557)
body:
A reference action matched inside a word, so `prefix` gave a reference the `fix` action,
and a word starting with a keyword, like `fixups`, ended the sentence of the previous
action without starting a new one, so the references after it were lost. Keywords now
match as whole words only.

References that got an action by mistake have none now, and the dropped ones come back,
which the cli test now expects.

subject: declare DEFAULT_COMMIT_TYPES and format function exports (#1552)
replace `semver` with `verkit` (#1555)
body:
verkit follows node-semver semantics with typed, ESM, zero-dependency functions, so
`@types/semver` goes away too.

Two call sites cannot be swapped by name. `getPrerelease` returns an empty array for a
stable version where `prerelease` returned `null`, so `isPrereleaseVersion` uses
`isPrerelease` instead. And verkit takes a value that is not a string for an already parsed
version, which makes `isValid(undefined)` true, so the writer checks that the version is a
string before it validates it.

subject: fail loudly when a preset is rendered by an old writer (#1539)
body:
conventional-changelog-writer@8 and older compile a handlebars mainTemplate
string, which modern presets no longer provide. In a mixed versions install,
e.g. the preset hoisted to the latest major next to tooling that bundles
writer@8, the writer silently fell back to its default template and produced
a changelog with empty sections.

Presets now plant a mainTemplate which throws a self-describing error when
an old writer renders it. Modern writers have no such option and ignore it.

closes #1495

subject: add conventional-commits-filter to dependencies (#1536)
body:
ConventionalGitClient#loadDeps() unconditionally imports both
conventional-commits-parser and conventional-commits-filter on the
getCommits() path, but only the parser was declared as a dependency.
The filter was reachable only through git-client's optional peer
dependency, which npm 11 prunes from the install (npm/cli#9249),
causing ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND at runtime during changelog generation.

subject: end the options list before caller provided values (#1535)
body:
A value starting with a dash was parsed by git as an option, so
`checkout('--pathspec-from-file=/tmp/secret')` made git read that file and
report its lines in the error output, which `exec` turns into the message of
the thrown error. A commits or tags range could reach `git log --output=<file>`
and write the log to an arbitrary path.

`--end-of-options` is used rather than `--`: in `git checkout` the latter means
that pathspecs follow, which is why it was removed in 993c1fdd, and restoring
it would break branch switching again.

subject: use current host url paths (#1534)
body:
GitLab removed the urls without the `-/` separator in 16.0, so every commit,
issue and comparison link generated for GitLab pointed at a legacy path.

Host configs now carry the comparison path as well, and both presets read the
issue path from the context instead of hardcoding it. Bitbucket issue links
follow along: its config still used the legacy singular `issue` path.

Fixes #986.

subject: group notes by their keyword (#1533)
body:
Both presets rewrote the title of every note to `BREAKING CHANGES`, so a custom
parser `noteKeywords` entry — `SECURITY`, for example — ended up in the breaking
changes section and counted as a breaking change when recommending a version.

Notes are now grouped by their own keyword: breaking change spellings are merged
into a single group, any other keyword becomes a group of its own, and only
breaking changes affect the recommended bump. The conventionalcommits preset gets
`formatNoteTitle` and `formatNoteIcon` to rename groups and to put an icon in
front of them.

Fixes #815.

subject: format references in breaking change notes (#1529)
body:
Issue references were formatted in commit subjects only, so `issuePrefixes`
and `formatIssueUrl` had no effect on breaking change notes.

Both presets now share `createReferencesFormatter` from the template package
and apply it to notes and subjects. It keeps already formatted Markdown as is:
links, bare urls, fenced code blocks and single-line code spans.

This changes existing output: notes with the default `#` prefix are linked now,
and references inside code spans, links and urls in subjects are no longer
replaced.

Fixes #631.

```diff
subject: Fix flaky ConnectionController retry tests (#136527)
body:
Provisioning: Fix flaky ConnectionController retry tests

The retry tests advance a fake queue clock once and then block in
queue.Get(). client-go's delaying queue builds its timer relative to the
clock's current time, so a Step that lands between waitingLoop reading the
time and creating the timer is lost. Nothing steps again, and the test hangs
until the package timeout. Keep stepping until the delayed retry is enqueued,
and fail after 5s instead of hanging.

subject: Fix flaky Zanzana reconcile barrier in legacy mode (#136505)
body:
Tests: Await two Zanzana reconcile cycles in legacy reconcile barrier

AwaitZanzanaReconcileNext returned as soon as the last-success timestamp
passed the baseline taken after the caller's write. A cycle already in
flight when the write happened could finish first, so the barrier released
before any cycle had observed the new permissions, causing intermittent 403s
(e.g. TestIntegrationDashboardAPIZanzanaCrossOrg root dashboard by Editor).
Wait for two completions so the second is guaranteed to have started after
the baseline.

Since the build image bump to git 2.55, auto maintenance (which uses the
"geometric" strategy by default since git 2.54) writes a commit-graph in
the angle checkout of the Linux-built src cache. That graph lists commits
that only exist in the alternates git cache, so once fix_angle_git removes
the alternates, git fetch aborts on mac and Windows with "which is in the
commit graph file but not in the object database". Remove the commit-graph
together with the alternates.

subject: validate asar header and entry sizes against the archive length (#55171)
body:
The native asar reader now checks the header size field against the
archive's actual length before reading it, and treats file entries whose
size is negative or whose offset + size runs past the end of the archive
as missing. Previously these values were used as-is, so a truncated or
otherwise malformed archive could make fs calls fail in confusing ways
instead of reporting an invalid package / ENOENT like the JS
implementation in @electron/asar does.

subject: restore tray tooltip when explorer restarts on Windows (#54624)
body:
When the taskbar is re-created, NotifyIcon::ResetIcon() re-added the
icon without its tooltip, because SetToolTip() did not keep a copy.
Screen readers use the tooltip as the name of the notification area
button, so after an explorer restart they announced only "button".

Store the tooltip and send it with NIF_TIP when the icon is re-added.

subject: crash when onSendHeaders observes a Blob upload (#55085)
body:
* fix: crash when onSendHeaders observes a Blob upload

For a request that only observer webRequest listeners match,
ObservedURLLoader posted a copy of the request to the UI thread while
the IO thread sent the original to the network. Both copies shared one
ResourceRequestBody, so the UI thread cloned a Blob element's data pipe
getter for uploadData while the IO thread cloned the same getter to
serialize the request. Cloning takes the getter out of its element for
the duration of the call, so when the two overlapped one thread called
Clone through an empty remote and the main process crashed.

subject: deliver extension events to service workers (#55146)
body:
Extension service workers register their event listeners with the

for frames. Listeners added in a worker were never registered, so events
such as storage.onChanged and alarms.onAlarm never reached it.

subject: update Node.js release schedule (#47417)
body:
* feat(static-data): update Node.js release schedule

Changed:

- `v27`

* fix(versioning/node): read `lts` for Node.js 27+ schedule entries

As seen in e8eb125ce3fe6d4ab6297640283f91d6909cb36f, the upstream
schedule for `v27` now provides the LTS date as `lts` rather than
`maintenance`. `isStable` special-cased entries with an `alpha` date to
read `maintenance`, so it found no date for `v27`, and treated every
`27.x` release as unstable, even after the LTS date had passed.

As `lts` is now the LTS-promotion date for every entry, we can drop the
special case and always read `lts`.

subject: extract `runs.image` in Docker container actions (#47423)
body:
When a GitHub Action uses a pre-built Docker container in its
`runs.image`, we didn't previously extract + suggest updates.

As Actions should really be digest pinning these container images, we
should make it easier for maintainers to keep these updated by
extracting + updating it.

We only need to extract this when there's a `docker://` prefix, and
ignore local i.e. `Dockerfile` references.

As the runner matches the `docker://` prefix case-insensitively[0], we
do the same, although this doesn't change the existing (case-sensitive)
handling of `uses: docker://...`.

subject: notify all active shared observable subscribers (#7729)
body:
## Why

- `share()` iterates a live observer array. A subscriber's terminal
notification triggers its teardown, which splices that array and skips
the next subscriber.
- For example, with two active subscribers, an upstream `complete()`
only completes the first. A subscriber that unsubscribes in `next()` can
also make another subscriber miss a value.

subject: don't hang when the node request body was already consumed (#7706)
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
Confidence: high — a single branch that only runs for an ended stream
without `req.body` (which previously always hung); full CI green.

Fixes #5534

## Root cause

`createBody` in
`packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/incomingMessageToRequest.ts`
only checked `req.readableEnded` when `req` had a `body` property. When
another middleware drained the request stream without setting `req.body`
(e.g. `@koa/bodyparser` without `patchNode`), it attached `data`/`end`
listeners to a stream that had already ended, so any procedure reading
its input waited forever.

subject: stream the request body when express 5 body-parser leaves req.body undefined (#7447)
body:
Closes #7446

## 🎯 Changes

Bug fix. Express 5's body-parser defines `req.body` (as `undefined`)
even on content types it skips, e.g. `multipart/form-data`.
`createBody`'s `'body' in req` presence check then treated such requests
as pre-parsed and built a body-less `Request`, so `request.formData()`
failed with `Failed to parse body as FormData` for anyone running
express 5 (including every NestJS app) with global body parsers
registered.

`createBody` now only treats the request as pre-parsed when `req.body`
holds a value. When the property exists but is `undefined`, it returns
an empty body

subject: only abort node-http requests when the connection closes early (#7664)
body:
Closes #7663

## 🎯 Changes

Bug fix. `incomingMessageToRequest` aborted the request's
`AbortController` on the response's `close` event. `close` is also
emitted after a response that was sent completely, so every successful
request ended with `ac.abort()`, and `opts.signal` in a procedure
reported an abort the client never made.

The `close` listener now only aborts when the response hasn't been ended
yet (`res.writableEnded` is false), i.e. when the connection went away
before the response was written. A completed response just removes the
`aborted` listener. `req`'s `aborted` event still abo

subject: clear the sse maxDurationMs timer when the subscription ends (#7666)
body:
Related to #7663

## 🎯 Changes

With `sse.maxDurationMs` set, `resolveResponse` starts a timer for each
subscription and only clears it when the request signal aborts. If the
signal never aborts, the timer stays pending for the full
`maxDurationMs` and keeps its closure and the event loop alive. That
happens when:

- the generator returns
- the procedure throws before streaming (e.g. in a middleware)
- the response body is cancelled
- `responseMeta` throws while the SSE response is being built
- the SSE stream errors (e.g. `onError` throws while an error is being
formatted)

subject: hash only the root pnpm-lock.yaml for the pnpm cache key (#7695)
body:
## Why

- `actions/cache` in `./.github/setup` builds its key from
`hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml')`. Its post-job step works out that
expression again after `pnpm install`, when the glob also has to walk
all of `node_modules`.
```

Bug fix. `getQueryKeyInternal` checks `!input` when it builds an `any`
key, so every falsy input (`0`, `false`, `''`, `null`) gets treated as

## Summary

Lazy router keys are dotted-path prefixes, and a procedure nested under
a key resolves as `key + '.' + rest`. `getProcedureAtPath` picks the

body:
Header names on the HTTP/1 fast path in `Deno.serve` reach the
propagator carrier verbatim from the wire, so a request with
`Traceparent:` (or any non-lowercase spelling) was silently ignored and
the server span started a fresh trace instead of joining the caller's.
HTTP/2 was unaffected because hyper already normalises header names
there.

The fix just lowercases the names when building the carrier array. The
new spec test sends a raw HTTP/1.1 request over TCP, since `fetch`
lowercases header names itself and can't reproduce this.

body:
Adds `navigator.clipboard` (text only) to `deno desktop`, mirroring the
web
[Clipboard
API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Clipboard).

## What it does

- Exposes `navigator.clipboard` as a real `Clipboard` (extends
`EventTarget`),
installed as a `[SameObject]` prototype getter on `Navigator` — matching
how
the built-in `Navigator` attributes are defined (webidl-branded
receiver).
- Implements the async text methods:
- `readText(): Promise<string>` — resolves to the clipboard text, or
`""`

subject: preserve keep-alive after reading request body (#36690)
body:
Fixes #36657.

The raw HTTP/1 server path treated every non-prebuffered request body as
non-reusable, even after JavaScript had reached end-of-stream. Track
when the JS reader finishes, preserve keep-alive only after the reader
releases the connection, and drain any cancelled remainder before
parsing the next pipelined request. Unread and in-flight bodies still
close the connection.

Motivation: With tags v1.0.0, v1.0 and v1 on one commit, the scm version
provider returned "1.0". The three versions compare equal, and max()

unchanged.

string and aborted with  atal: ambiguous argument, breaking every

os.path.expandvars so the hook keeps working without reintroducing
shell execution. Unset variables are left literal so git surfaces a

body:
When queries timeout on the GitHub backend we experience 502 errors.
Automatically reduce pagination size when encountering
intermittent 502 Bad Gateway GraphQL timeouts to ensure resilient
history retrieval.
- Halve pagination size (`opts.num`) on each caught 502 error retry attempt.
- Force pagination size to exactly 1 on the final retry attempt to maximize successful recovery.
- Ensure pagination size never drops below 1 on earlier attempts.

subject: add timeout parameter to to_dataframe and to_arrow met… (#2354)
body:
### Description

This PR adds a `timeout` parameter to the `to_dataframe()` and
`to_arrow()` methods (and their corresponding `*_iterable`,
`*_geodataframe` and `QueryJob` wrappers) in the BigQuery client
library.

This addresses an issue where these methods could hang indefinitely if
the underlying BigQuery Storage API stream blocked (e.g., due to
firewall issues or network interruptions) during the download phase. The
added `timeout` parameter ensures that the download operation respects
the specified time limit and raises a `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError`
if it exceeds the duration.

argument to the superclass, ensuring that the provided retry settings
are always honored.

A new test case is added to verify that `job.result()` correctly
handles both the default retry and a custom retry object.

subject: specify the inherited-members directive for job classes (#2244)
body:
It seems that versions of python earlier than 3.10 may have had issues
processing inherited members annotations, and accidentally include
inherited members by default.

As we recently worked to excise older versions of python in this repo,
it seems we're now correctly processing sphinx directives, which means
we no longer emit docstrings for inherited members.

This PR adds a minor sphinx directive to include inherited members
for the job classes, and I've confirmed locally by running the `docsfx`
nox job that the inherited members do now get included in the docfx_yaml
output.

subject: use URL-safe base64 for the feature tracking header (#20684)
body:
## Problem

`x-goog-storage-go-features` is encoded with `encodeUint32` (standard
base64, shared with CRC32C), but the server decodes this header with a
strict web-safe base64 decoder (RFC 4648 §5) that rejects `+` and `/`.
Any bitmask whose encoding contains those characters — e.g. features 3–7
or 9–13 all set — would be silently dropped server-side as more features
are tracked. Today's two features cannot trigger it, so this is a latent
bug.

## Changes

- Add `encodeFeatureMask` / `decodeFeatureMask` in `tracker.go` using
`base64.URLEncoding`. The decoder is lenient (URL-safe **or** standar

(representing the unique identifier for a resumable upload session) to

subject: keep flatten validation on the tagged field (#20659)
body:
`validateChildType` copied a field's flatten option into the loop
variable. Every sibling declared after that field was then validated as
flattened. A nested slice in that position was rejected as a slice of
slices. Declaring the flattened field last saved the same struct.

The option now applies only to the field it is declared on. A slice that
is itself marked flatten still fails, which is the nested
slice-of-slices case.

subject: roll back transaction when RunInTransaction callback panics (#20674)
body:
Fixes #5969

### Summary
Ensures `Client.RunInTransaction` rolls back the active transaction if
the user-provided callback `f` panics before allowing the panic to
continue unwinding.

### Details
Previously, if `f(tx)` panicked during `RunInTransaction`, execution
unwound past `tx.rollbackWithRetry()`, leaving the transaction open on
the server until its lock timed out. Using a `defer` around `f(tx)`
ensures `tx.rollbackWithRetry()` is called when `f` panics while
preserving the original panic and stack trace.

expires — ~925 s with the default `net.ipv4.tcp_retries2=15` — and
**indefinitely** if the dead peer's host still answers bare TCP
keepalive ACKs (no kernel timer fires). Application‑layer PINGs are the
only client‑side mechanism that detects this case; they close the
connection within ~`Time+Timeout` so the client's retry logic can fail
over.

subject: disable DirectPath fallback by default (#20648)
body:
#14414 enabled the DirectPath to CloudPath fallback by default for
clients that enable DirectPath.

The fallback connection pool sends each request to the next channel in
round-robin order, so the requests of a read-write transaction do not
stay on the same channel. With DirectPath, each channel is connected to
a single Spanner frontend, so most requests of a read-write transaction
are forwarded to the transaction owner. This happens for every
transaction, not only after a fallback has occurred.

Fallback is rarely used (~ 1 in 4000 requests), so this change disables
it by default. It can stil

subject: update BufferPool Get/TryGet semantics (#20647)
body:
Updates the experimental BufferPool interface (added in #20513 and
#20522) to match the revised design:

- `Get(maxSize)` is non-blocking and always returns a buffer regardless
of pool constraints (error only on allocation failure). It no longer
takes a context. Callers use it for the first buffer of each upload to
guarantee progress and avoid deadlocks.
- `TryGet(maxSize)` now returns `([]byte, bool, error)`: `false` when a
buffer cannot be provided within the pool's constraints, error only on
allocation failure.

The interface is still unsupported; this only changes the API surface.

subject: correct remaining bytes for gRPC bidi range reads (#20619)
body:
## Description
For gRPC BiDi range reads (`WithGRPCBidiReads`), the expected byte count
was computed as `length - startOffset`, treating the requested length as
an end offset. Range reads at a non-zero offset therefore:
- logged a bogus `received N more bytes than requested` on `Close()`,
where N equals the read offset.
- returned a wrong `Reader.Remain()`.

The data read was always correct.

## Changes
- New `rangeReaderRemain` helper: `min(length, size - startOffset)`,
never below 0.
- Used by the BiDi range reader, and as the `ReadObject` fallback when
the response has no `ContentRange`.

subject: prioritize leader replica for read-write transactions in location-aware routing (#20620)
body:
When location-aware routing is enabled, read-write requests that prefer
the leader could be routed to a follower because a non-zero operation
UID on the routing hint sent fillRoutingHintAttempt down the score-aware
replica selection path before the local leader was considered. There the
leader only receives a cost bias, so a sufficiently faster follower
would win.

Check for a healthy local leader first whenever preferLeader is set, and
fall back to score-aware selection only when the leader is missing,
remote, or unhealthy. This mirrors googleapis/google-cloud-java#14195.

subject: Auto enable mTLS when supported certificates are detected (#1637)
body:
The Python SDK will use a hybrid approach for mTLS enablement:

If the GOOGLE_API_USE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE environment variable is set
(either true or false or any value), the SDK will respect that setting.
This is necessary for test scenarios and users who need to explicitly
control mTLS behavior.
If the GOOGLE_API_USE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE environment variable is not
set, the SDK will automatically enable mTLS only if it detects Managed
Workload Identity (MWID) or X.509 Workforce Identity Federation (WIF)
certificate sources. In other cases where the variable is not set, mTLS
will remain disabled

subject: send each MySQL statement in one round trip, with the mariadb package substituting values (#30918)
body:
## At a glance

The MySQL adapter renders:

```sql
SELECT `id` FROM `user` WHERE `role` = ?1 LIMIT ?2
-- params: ['ADMIN', 10]
```

Before this PR the driver prepared the statement on the server, waited
for the reply, then executed it: two round trips per query. Now it hands
the SQL and values to the `mariadb` package's `query`, which writes the
values in and sends the statement once:

```sql
SELECT `id` FROM `user` WHERE `role` = 'ADMIN' LIMIT 10
```

A live test counts the commands MySQL receives: one per statement, no
prepares.

## What this PR changes

1. Both MySQL drivers send every stat

subject: run the MySQL drivers on the mariadb package, with every value in a prepared statement (#30893)
body:
## At a glance

The MySQL adapter renders a query whose parameter appears twice:

```sql
SELECT `id` FROM `post` WHERE `author_id` = ?1 OR `editor_id` = ?1 LIMIT ?2
-- params: [7, 10]
```

The driver now runs it on the `mariadb` package as a server-side
prepared statement:

```sql
SELECT `id` FROM `post` WHERE `author_id` = ? OR `editor_id` = ? LIMIT ?
-- values sent separately: [7n, 7n, 10n]   (BIGINT)
```

The values never enter the SQL text. Integers are sent as BIGINT, so
`LIMIT ?` works without a `CAST`.

The MySQL drivers now copy the Postgres driver's patterns,

on it afterwards. When a parallel run spawns its scripts from several

subject: close each libsql connection once (#17366)
body:
Windows Rust CI aborted pnpr-auth libsql tests with 0xc0000005 (four
times recently: registration_cap_is_strict_across_backend_instances
three times, sync_server::bulk_revocation_refreshes_a_replica_whose_tokens_went_elsewhere
once).

libsql's LibsqlConnection::drop calls disconnect() and then the inner
local::Connection's own Drop calls disconnect() again. Both see the
drop_ref Arc as unique, so sqlite3_close_v2 runs a second time on a
handle SQLite already freed. Usually it reads freed memory as "closed"
and reports misuse. When another thread reused that memory, it read
garbage and crashed.

subject: reject forbidden sequences in query comments (#8536)
body:
`qb.comment()` and `qb.hintComment()` document `/*`, `*/` and `?` as
forbidden, but since the knex removal in v7 nothing enforced it (knex
threw on these). A `*/` ends the comment block early and corrupts the
statement, and a `?` is consumed by the parameter formatter, so the
first bound value lands inside the comment and every following
placeholder shifts.

The check now lives in the `NativeQueryBuilder` setters, so the query
builder, the `comments`/`hintComments` find options and direct native
builder usage all throw up front with the same error, matching the 6.x
behaviour.

body:
Closes #8489

`PostgreSqlSchemaHelper.parseIndexColumnsFromExpression` finds each
column's modifiers (`DESC`, `NULLS …`, `COLLATE …`) with a pattern that
isn't anchored. For `id` in `author_id, created_at DESC, id DESC`, it
matches the end of `author_id` first, reads empty modifiers, and so

the index on every schema update.

The pattern now matches the column as a whole list item: it must be
preceded by the start of the list or a comma, and followed by

subject: refuse to commit when rolling back to a savepoint failed (#8462)
body:
When a nested `transactional()` fails and its `rollback to savepoint`
fails too, the rollback error is only logged. If the caller catches the
inner error and keeps going, the outer `commit` goes through and takes
the inner writes with it, even though they were supposed to be rolled
back.

The failed savepoint rollback is now recorded on the parent transaction,
and committing it throws instead (with the rollback error as `cause`).
The outer `transactional()` then rolls back as a whole. The inner
callback still rejects with its own error, as before.

Fixes #8458

Co-authored-by: Marti

pg_sleep(5)` runs. PostgreSQL only notices the closed socket once the
sleep ends and it tries to send the result, so that backend stays in the
database for about 5 seconds. `DROP DATABASE` waits up to 5 seconds for
other sessions, so the drop raced against it. Bumping the sleep to 10s
made it fail every time. The test now terminates that backend at the

subject: reject a commit PostgreSQL answered with ROLLBACK (#8499)
body:
PostgreSQL doesn't raise when `COMMIT` runs in an aborted transaction
(e.g. after a caught unique violation). It answers with the command tag
`ROLLBACK`, and Kysely drops the tag, so `em.transactional()` and
`em.commit()` resolved even though every write was discarded. This still
happens with kysely 0.29.7.

The pool now uses a `pg.Client` subclass that rejects a `commit`
answered with `ROLLBACK`. Kysely then treats it like any other failed
commit (a deferred constraint violation, say), and the existing rollback
releases the connection.

body:
kysely's `ControlledTransaction` only releases its connection after a
successful `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` (kysely-org/kysely#1990). When the server

resolves.

client back to the pool (with the error, so `pg-pool` discards it).

subject: drop nx's undici override (#8437)
body:
The `undici@npm:7.29.0` override from #8433 only silenced Dependabot for
the undici nx pins. It costs more than it's worth: Renovate can't
regenerate `yarn.lock` for that version-scoped key, so every bump it
opens fails CI (#8434, #8436), and #8436 sits in the automerged
non-major group, blocking every other patch/minor update.

nx is a dev-only dependency here (through lerna), and it only loads
undici when proxy env vars are set. This drops the override along with
the Renovate rule from #8435.

subject: keep renovate from bumping the undici override to v8 (#8435)
body:
Renovate treats `resolutions` entries as regular deps. The
`undici@npm:7.29.0` → `7.29.1` override from #8433 (it patches nx's
pinned undici) was read as "undici 7.29.1", so #8434 tried to bump it to
8.11.2. That would push nx onto a new undici major. Renovate also
couldn't regenerate `yarn.lock` for the descriptor-scoped key, so every
job failed on the immutable install.

This caps the undici override at `<8`. Renovate can still offer 7.x
patches, and #8434 should auto-close once this lands.

fixes either pin yet (lerna 10.1.0 bumps handlebars, but it's only on

7.29.1. The undici override only targets the `7.29.0` descriptor, so
node-gyp's undici 6 and 8 copies don't change.

subject: insert on upsert without a unique value (#8398)
body:
`em.upsert()` on MongoDB with nothing to identify an existing document
(for example a nullable unique property set to `null` and no `_id`) ran
`updateMany({}, { $set }, { upsert: true })`. The empty filter matches

returned first.

`MongoDriver.nativeUpdate` now inserts when an upsert has an empty
condition and returns the new `_id`, so the entity gets its own primary

subject: don't infer `defineEntity` properties from index `where` and key options (#8395)
body:
When `properties` is a callback (`p => ({ ... })`), TS defers its
inference and picks up `TProperties` from the keys in
`indexes[].where`/`uniques[].where` instead. A partial index like `{
properties: ['booking'], where: { current: true } }` was then rejected,
because `booking` isn't a key of the `where` object.

The `where` types are now wrapped in `NoInfer`, same as `properties` and
`include` already were. `versionProperty`, `serializedPrimaryKey`,
`concurrencyCheckKeys` and `primaryKeys` had the same problem and get
the same fix.

Closes #8394

body:
This only affects drivers without pivot tables (MongoDB). SQL drivers

subject: replace reactive Set/Map state on hydration instead of unioning it (#3162)
body:
* fix(store): replace reactive Set/Map state on hydration instead of unioning it

When a setup store's state contains a reactive(new Set()) / reactive(new Map())
with default entries, hydrating from server state unioned the two collections
instead of replacing them, so defaults the server had removed survived. The
sibling ref() branch and HMR both replace, and the server state is authoritative.

Clear the reactive Set/Map before merging in the hydration path only, leaving
$patch's own merge semantics unchanged. The existing hydration tests used empty
defaults, so they never exercised this.

body:
The shouldHydrate predicate short-circuited to "do hydrate" for any value
that failed isPlainObject, so the marker added by skipHydrate() was silently
ignored on refs to non-plain reactive containers such as Map, Set, arrays,
and class instances. Broaden the check so the marker is honoured on any
non-null object while keeping null/primitive safety.

body:
With `{ "/docs/**": { headers: false }, "/docs/x/**": { headers: { csp } } }`,
`/docs/x%2fy` lost the CSP header: the served path's broader `false` reset
`headers`, and a permissive rule was never re-added from another reading
even when a narrower pattern matched it there.

- rules: resets record the routes that reset each rule; a later reading may
  reinstate a permissive rule only when its pattern is equal to or more
  specific than every resetting route (`canOverride`); restricting rules
  still always re-add; no predicate keeps the old behavior
- rules: resolve all readings before unioning

subject: normalize rule keys like routes and tighten the shape guard
body:
Rule keys could fail open against the route registered from the same
string. `decodeRoutePattern` decoded `%7B` `%7D` `%3F` `%5E` into rou3
syntax (`/%7Bq%7D/a` became the group `/{q}/a`), decoded escapes inside
regex constraints, left raw constraint text unencoded, merged non-ASCII
into a param name (`/:idé`), and kept dot segments unresolved.

- rules: a rule key is now the `normalizeRoute` fixpoint, identical to the
  route, so a key always matches its own route's spelling
- rules: uppercase/lowercase hex recasings of the request path are
  ordinary union-only alternate readings (they add r

subject: update rou3 to v0.12
body:
- middleware: literal fast path only accepts text rou3 stores verbatim (rou3 now percent-encodes `^`, space, non-ASCII, ... in pattern literals; `use("/a^b/**")` missed `/a%5Eb/...`)
- middleware: `**` binds `{ 0, _ }` and nothing when it takes no segment
- rules: look up the decoded reading both re-encoded (rou3 encodes pattern literals) and raw (regex constraints stay as written)
- rules: shape guard fails closed on groups; drop the zero-matchable carve-out (`:x*` is now contained in `**`)
- test: `*` is a greedy catch-all and a route allows one catch-all
- docs: `*` / `**` catch-all semanti

subject: prevent duplicate derived subscriptions on reconnect (#18899)
body:
- A dirty disconnected derived registered newly reached dependencies
during evaluation, then `reconnect()` registered them again and retained
disposed graphs.
- The connection model from
[#17105](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/17105) and reconnection
added in [#17362](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/17362) restore
skipped old dependencies; recursive unfreezing from
[#17682](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/17682) requires
preserving that lifecycle.
- Made reconnection idempotent instead of skipping or moving it,
preserving unchanged subscriptions and frozen-effect order

subject: don't throw state_unsafe_mutation when the focused element is removed with bind:activeElement (#18921)
body:
Fixes #15742

With `<svelte:document bind:activeElement />`, clicking a button that
removes itself throws `state_unsafe_mutation`. Removing the focused
element makes the browser fire `focusout` while the `{#if}` block effect
is running, and the binding's listener sets the state from inside that
effect.

`bind_active_element` now calls `update` inside
`without_reactive_context`, like event handlers created with
`create_event` and `bind_window_scroll` already do.

subject: add note about `#key` in best-practices (#18851)
body:
We had this discussion with @teemingc about Astra using a key block as a
way to re-render the whole component, which is very inefficient.

When you think about it, a key block is actually almost never the right
solution unless you want, for example, to rerun the animations.

I propose to add this line here in the best practices skill/doc, which,
in my opinion, makes sense.

We should probably also add the same suggestions whenever we encounter a
key block in the MCP Auto Fixer. What do you think about it?

subject: ensure hydration state restoration for custom element attribute updates (#18467)
body:
### Problem
While hydrating custom elements, set_attributes temporarily disables
global hydration state via set_hydrating(false) and restores it only at
the end. If a prop setter or attribute operation throws partway through,
hydration mode can remain disabled globally.

### Fix
Wrap the temporary hydration-state override in a try/finally block in
set_attributes so set_hydrating(true) always runs when
is_hydrating_custom_element is true.

body:
`{const item = 1}` inside `{#snippet row(item)}` compiles, and the
output declares `item` twice in one function, so it does not parse:

```js
const row = ($$anchor, item = $.noop) => {
	const item = 1;
```

`{let}`, `{@const}` and a nested snippet with the parameter's name do
the same. In `phases/scope.js`, `EachBlock` visits its body's children
in the item's own scope, so a tag that reuses the item name is a
`declaration_duplicate`. `SnippetBlock` calls `context.next({ scope:
child_scope })`, the `Fragment` visitor opens another scope for the
body, and the tag never meets the parameter.

subject: keep a reactive assignment with no dependencies when `migrate` cannot turn it into a declaration (#18817)
body:
`migrate()` dropped a reactive assignment that has no dependencies and
put nothing in its place:

```svelte
$: count = 7;          →  (gone, `{count}` now undeclared)
$: obj.x = 1;          →  (gone)
```

A binding the statement declares now always gets its `let`, and the
statement is only removed once every target has one; otherwise it
becomes `run()`:

```svelte
let count = $state(7);
run(() => { obj.x = 1; });
```

subject: don't hang `migrate` on a declaration that shares a line with its script tag (#18816)
body:
`migrate()` never returned when a declaration shared a line with its
`<script>` tag:

```svelte
<script>export let answer</script>
```

The scan that removes a migrated `export let` line looked for a newline
in both directions with no bound. It now stops at the script's edges.

body:
Closes #13864

A `let:` directive on a component only applies to the default slot
content. If the content is an explicit `{#snippet children()}` block,

```svelte
</Child>
```

This adds a compile error on the directive that points to snippet
parameters instead (`{#snippet children({ value })}`, or `{ item: x }`
for `let:item={x}`). Components with a `slot` attribute are not
affected, since there the directive applies to t

subject: don't warn about redundant `link` role on `<area>` without `href` (#18872)
body:
Since #11737, `<a role="link">` without an `href` no longer triggers
`a11y_no_redundant_roles`, but `<area role="link">` without an `href`
still does. Per [ARIA in
HTML](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-area-no-href), an `<area>`
without `href` has the implicit role `generic` and `link` is one of its
allowed roles, so the role isn't redundant. This applies the existing
`<a>` exception to `<area>` and adds test cases for `<area>` with and
without `href`.

Closes #9261. The `<a>` example in that issue was already fixed by
#11737, but the issue was left open.

subject: don't overwrite an unchanged spread `value` (#18864)
body:
Fixes #18862

When a `value` is applied through a spread (`<input {...props} />`),
`set_attributes` always writes `element.value`, even if the element
already has that value. Writing `value` on a number input clears any
incomplete text: typing `250.` makes `input.value` `''` (the text is

then becomes `''` too, writing `''` erases what the user typed.

This is what happens with SvelteKit remote forms:
`fields.quantity.as('number')` coerces `''` to `undefined`, the spread
`value` becomes `''`, and Svelte writes it back to t

subject: resolve the fallback of an each block in the enclosing scope (#18803)
body:
In `phases/scope.js`, `EachBlock` visits `node.fallback` with the
block's own scope, so `{:else}` resolves the loop's name to the each
context. With `let item = $state('outer')` outside and `{#each items as
item}…{:else}<button onclick={() => (item = 'changed')}>` the compiler
reports "Cannot reassign or bind to each block argument" for a variable
that is not the block's argument.

The fallback renders when there is nothing to iterate, so it is visited
in the enclosing scope, as an await block's `pending` is.

not defined`. Server rendering kept the binding.

puts the `let` / `const` form on the same path as `$state.snapshot`.

timing of microtasks, or during flushing effects are scheduling new

subject: remove `WAS_MARKED` flag in favor of `Set` (#18127)
body:
Removes the `WAS_MARKED` logic in favor of a simple `Set` heuristic: If
`mark_reactions` goes beyond a certain count, initialize it, otherwise
keep it `null`. Balances the common case of not having many transitive
dependencies with the edge case of cyclic dependencies as was seen in
#16658 (I rechecked that reproduction and it remains fast with this
change).

I ran the benchmark against this and it doesn't hit the `Seen` heuristic
once (i.e. even the benchmark doesn't have this extreme level of
dependencies where it becomes noticeable).

Fixes #18123, supersedes #18124

After #18738 the biggest thing left in the parser profile was acorn's
constructor, `getOptions` and `wordsRegexp` alone were around 12% of
parse time. `parseExpressionAt` is `new Parser()` followed by
`parseExpression()`, and we call it for every expression in the
template. For something like `{name}` the constructor (normalizing
options, four keyword regexes, scope state) is about 2 µs while the
actual parse is under 1 µs, and components have dozens of these.

The fix seemed to belong in acorn, cache the options and regexes so
repeated `parseExpressionAt` calls stop redoing them. I lasted abo

subject: stop scanning the whole template for every expression (#18738)
body:
Parsing a 90 KB component drops from 460 ms to 35 ms; typical components
parse ~30% faster.

`read_pattern` blanked out the entire template before the pattern with
`replace(/[^\n]/g, ' ')` to keep positions aligned, and
`acorn.parseExpressionAt` re-counted lines from the top of the file on
every call. Acorn never looks before `pos`, so the real template can be
the prefix, and acorn 8.18's `startLocation` takes the line we already
have from the locator.

The blanking also had `loc.column` off by one for every node inside a
destructured pattern (noted in #18087), hence the snapshot updates.

subject: don't export JSON keys that the finalizer inlines away from a shared chunk (#11396)
body:
When a JSON dynamic entry is in a common chunk (top-level await or
`chunkOptimization: false` turns off the merge), its facade chunk
imported every export of the entry. That included keys that the
finalizer folds into the default-export object, so the common chunk
exported `k` without a declaration and Node rejected it.

The finalizer, the #10020 export filter, and the cross-chunk liveness
check now use one predicate for an inlined JSON key.

fixes #11392

body:
When module-level code reads a `var` before its declaration, the read sees `undefined`, but rolldown inlines the initializer's value into it. This PR stops inlining such a `var`.

```js

```

Run unbundled, this prints `undefined`. Before, the bundle contains `console.log(true)`. After, the read stays `console.log(flag)`.

```
An inlined common chunk is printed as a factory passed to `__share(id, (exports) => { … })`. subject: incremental cycle check for `avoidRedundantChunkLoads` (#11320)
body:
`optimize_dynamic_entry_bits` rebuilt the whole chunk graph to check each fold for a cycle, so its cost grew quadratically with the number of atoms. `ReducedChunkGraph` now builds the graph once and updates it with each move. Every edge a move adds starts or ends at the chunk that receives the atom, so while the graph is acyclic, one search from that chunk decides the move. A graph that already has a cycle gets a full check only for a move out of its single multi-chunk strongly connected component. The output is byte-identical to `main`.

closes #11262
```

Rolldown sizes its native Tokio runtime from the physical CPU count, which can describe the unrestricted host on Linux. An entry's public exports must stay unchanged when a dynamically
imported module dynamically imports one of the entry's static
dependencies. This PR adds a pure ESM regression test for the fix in

The fixture uses this import graph:

```text
main --static--> lib
main --dynamic--> adapter --dynamic--> lib
```

The built entry must retain only its declared `default` export, and both

subject: reduce instructions in SIMD byte searches (#28423)
body:
Perf optimization to byte searches, following on from #28387.

In the AVX2 version, the order of needles in needles arrays affects the
generated instructions. If two bytes which only differ in a single bit
are paired together, LLVM can check for those 2 bytes in 2 operations
instead of 3.

e.g. `<` and `>`:

- Separated: `(v == 0x3C) | (v == 0x3E)`  - 2 compares + 1 OR
- Paired: `(v & 0xFD) == 0x3C`  - 1 AND + 1 compare

(note the stack up to #28422 already did some refactoring after #28387)

subject: copy assets replaced by a rename in watch mode

When an asset is replaced by renaming another file over it, as editors with atomic
save do, the native file watcher on Linux reports the asset as added instead of
modified. The incremental build only copied existing assets that were reported as
modified, so the output kept the previous contents of the asset.

polling so that the native watcher is used.

`AngularServerApp.handle()` to reject via `promiseWithAbort`, while

The previous asset state was keyed by source file, so an asset copied to several destinations
(two asset entries with the same input, or one copy per locale with `localize`) kept only the last

Vitest browser runner sent an unquoted weak ETag such as `W/25a71cd345af2de4`. RFC 9110 requires
the entity tag to be quoted (`W/"25a71cd345af2de4"`), which is how the other ETags in the same
middleware are already formatted.

Fixes #34449

Because subproject dependencies (such as `@angular/core`) are omitted from this output, commands like `ng update` and `ng add` fail to detect installed project dependencies when executed in a Bun workspace member.

subject: type the external redirect guard (#33887)

`externalRedirect()` passed its guard to `canActivate` as an inline
arrow function. `canActivate` accepts `CanActivateFn` as well as the
deprecated class-based guards, typed as `ProviderToken<any>`. Any
function also matches `ProviderToken<any>`, so TypeScript didn't check
the inline guard against `CanActivateFn`. For example, a guard returning
a number would still compile.

`canActivate`, so its return value is type checked. The behavior is
unchanged. A comment explains why the type is needed, so it isn't
inlined again later.

## What is the current behavior?

Currently, the `ActivatedRoute` that `ion-router-outlet` injects into a

subject: exit 1, not 130, when dependents of a failed task are skipped (#37574)
body:
## Current Behavior

When a task fails and Nx skips the tasks that depend on it, `nx run`,
`nx run-many` and `nx affected` exit with 130 (the SIGINT code) instead
of 1.

Skipped tasks never go through `endTasks`, so they have no entry in the
`TaskResults` that `runTasksForCommand` collects. `didCommandComplete`
requires a result for every discrete task, sees the skipped ones
missing, and decides the run was interrupted. The same happens when a
batch runner reports all of its tasks as `skipped` (the `@nx/gradle`
case in the issue): the run exits 130 and nothing failed according to
the results.

remove fragment from schema $id values (#1332)
body:
Every schema/*.json declared a draft-07 $id with a fragment
(e.g. "release-it#release-it"). draft-07 requires the root $id to be an
absolute URI without a fragment, and because all five shared the base
"release-it", strict validators can't resolve the relative $refs
(e.g. "./git.json") against a fragment-bearing base.

Use distinct, fragment-free filename ids ("release-it.json", "git.json",
...) so the refs resolve and the base has no fragment.

subject: Replace @nodeutils/defaults-deep with defu for deep-default merging (#1297)
body:
* fix: replace @nodeutils/defaults-deep with defu

* Preserve defaultsDeep array-replace semantics with defu

Plain defu concatenates arrays from higher- and lower-priority layers,
which changes user-visible behavior for options like git.pushArgs,
git.commitArgs, npm.publishArgs, etc. Wrap defu with createDefu so a
user-provided array replaces the default instead of concatenating,
matching the previous @nodeutils/defaults-deep behavior.

Add tests covering array-valued override and empty-array clearing.

---------

Co-authored-by: Lars Kappert <lars@webpro.nl>
